NGA.note: Document states nothing on authentication services.
No link between civil register and ID system stated.
Only Benue technical issues with digital registration for displaced people; no national digital civil register status stated.
Cash assistance figures are UNHCR's own, not a government payment programme.
No population-wide ID share stated; only shares for displaced groups.
Nothing on who operates or owns the ID system.
No public register keyed on the national ID number stated.
Nothing on ID system biometrics, certification or population reach.

facts.fact: UNHCR, relayed by EUAA, says that in 2024 51.78% of IDPs and 46.01% of refugees and asylum seekers held legally recognised identity documents or credentials.
UNHCR, relayed by EUAA, says about 1,950 refugees in the South-South region were enrolled in state social registers, giving access to the Nigerian Identification Number and bank accounts.
UNHCR, relayed by EUAA, gives the share with a bank account in 2024 as 0.42% of IDPs and 29.22% of refugees and asylum seekers.

NGA.note: No statement on how local civil registration offices make records; Benue digital registration issue concerns displaced people only.
State social registers named only as an enrolment route for refugees; no programme MIS stated.
